data.description:
## Context

DSO's `detect-stack.sh` emits a single string (`python-poetry`, `ruby-rails`, `node-npm`, etc.) that conflates orthogonal axes — language, package manager, framework, infrastructure, CI platform, platforms-on-top. The flat schema cannot honestly describe a real project (a Strata Rails app on Terraform AWS deployed via GitHub Actions reduces to `ruby-rails`), and each pending first-class-platform epic (Java 70d5-37ee, Terraform jira-dig-1582, Jenkins jira-dig-1583, .NET ee22-4785, Azure DevOps 622a-3955, Strata Epic A2) compounds case-explosion in consumers that switch on the singular value. Polyglot projects cannot be represented at all. This epic migrates the schema to a namespaced flat array, preserving every existing value as an array element for back-compat, in-place across all consumers, with auto-migration of existing project configs and explicit in-session safety nets to mitigate the big-bang risk profile.

## In Scope

- Rewrite `plugins/dso/scripts/detect-stack.sh` to emit comma-separated namespaced array. Existing values (`python-poetry`, `ruby-rails`, `node-npm`, `golang`, `rust-cargo`, `ruby-jekyll`, `convention-based`, `unknown`) preserved as elements; atomic decompositions added (`python`, `ruby`, `node`, `go`, `rust`, `bundler`, `cargo`, `npm`, `poetry`, `rails`, `jekyll`); namespaced forms added (`language:ruby`, `package_manager:bundler`, `framework:rails`). When a compound value is detected, the array always includes both the compound form for back-compat AND every namespaced decomposition; the compound form is never suppressed.
- Author `plugins/dso/docs/DETECTION-SCHEMA.md`: namespaced-tag convention; axis enum (`language`, `package_manager`, `framework`, `infrastructure`, `ci`, `platform`, `build_system` — extensible); legacy-compound preservation rules; consumer query patterns; whitespace-strip rules; empty-value to `unknown` semantics; trailing-empty-element-strip; multi-`stack=` rejection at parse time; detector authoring guide.
- Update `plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` to v2: `stack` and `commands.*` schemas; v1 to v2 migration table; semicolon delimiter for `commands.*` documented.
- Migrate every legacy-pattern consumer in DSO from singular-equality to array-membership. Pre-migration inventory committed as `tests/audits/A0-stack-consumer-inventory.md` BEFORE any migration commit. Known consumers: `resolve-stack-adapter.sh:44`, `prefill-config.sh:138`, `project-detect.sh:346,348`. Inventory is the migration checklist; sprint stories sized one-per-consumer; `dso:completion-verifier` confirms checklist 100% before A0 closes.
- Add pre-commit hook `check-no-stack-case.sh` blocking future legacy patterns. Documented self-exclusion list covers the hook's own source, the synthetic-detector fixture, the schema doc's anti-pattern section; future tests use `# stack-case-exempt: <reason>` annotation.
- Auto-migrate existing project configs: when a v2-aware consumer reads `dso-config.conf` with legacy singular `stack=`, rewrite to v2 array using `flock` advisory file lock + `mktemp` + `mv` rename atomic write. Idempotent on v2 configs. Edge cases: missing trailing newline, malformed YAML rejected with named-line error, comments preserved, multiple `stack=` lines rejected, empty `stack=` migrated to single-element `unknown` array, read-only filesystem (EROFS) gracefully falls back to in-memory translation with `[DSO WARN]` log.
- Upgrade `commands.*` to multi-valued (semicolon `;` separator, NOT comma — chosen to avoid collision with comma-bearing command args like pytest `-k 'foo,bar'`): `commands.test_runner`, `commands.lint`, `commands.format`, `commands.format_check`, `commands.lint_ruff`, `commands.lint_mypy`. `commands.lint_ruff` and `commands.lint_mypy` are pre-existing single-valued keys being retrofitted; the polyglot fixture exercise is limited to `commands.test_runner` and `commands.lint`.
- Add `depends_on` link + one-line "blocked on A0" comment to each pending platform-integration epic: 70d5-37ee, jira-dig-1582, jira-dig-1583, ee22-4785, 622a-3955.
- Test fixtures (`tests/fixtures/stack-detection/`): one per existing stack value, two polyglot combinations (Python+JS, Ruby+Terraform), one Strata-anticipation fixture (`.template-application-rails/<name>.yml` with `_commit` + `_src_path`).
- Synthetic-detector behavioral test (`tests/fixtures/detect-fake.sh` + `tests/scripts/test-synthetic-detector.sh`): exercises new tag introduction AND collision case.
- Pre-cutover review checklist appended to the final commit's PR body for the deep-tier reviewer: audit clean, fixture tests green, round-trip tests green, smoke run green, inventory 100% checked, polyglot fixture executes both runners.

## Out of Scope

- Detector implementations for new platforms (Strata = Epic A2; Java, Terraform, Jenkins, .NET, Azure DevOps = the linked epics).
- Per-detection confidence scoring; per-detection source-file attribution; JSON/YAML detector output formats.
- Multi-runner CI orchestration logic; per-axis precedence rules at the detection layer.
- Renaming/restructuring `dso-config.conf` keys beyond the migration noted.
- Rollback escape hatch (env var) — declined; rollback is `git revert` of the release.
- CI cache invalidation logic for the mixed-state-during-partial-deploy scenario — release-notes guidance only.

## Success Criteria

1. Detection emits namespaced array per fixture, including Strata-anticipation. Running `detect-stack.sh` against each fixture in `tests/fixtures/stack-detection/` (eight existing stack values + two polyglot combinations + one Strata-anticipation fixture) produces a comma-separated array matching golden-master assertions in `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md`. The Strata-anticipation fixture (with `.template-application-rails/<name>.yml`) plus a stub Strata detector together produce an array containing `ruby,bundler,rails,ruby-rails,language:ruby,package_manager:bundler,framework:rails,framework:strata-rails,platform:strata`. End-to-end smoke test runs `validate.sh --ci` against the polyglot fixture (Python+JS) AND asserts the emitted stack array contains exactly `{python, ruby, poetry, bundler, python-poetry, ruby-rails, language:python, language:ruby, package_manager:poetry, package_manager:bundler, framework:rails}`. The multi-command iteration path through `commands.test_runner` is exercised (both `pytest` and `npm test` execute and report separately). Verified by `tests/scripts/test-detect-stack-fixtures.sh` passing in CI.

2. All consumers migrated; existing configs auto-migrate idempotently. Pre-migration inventory `tests/audits/A0-stack-consumer-inventory.md` enumerates every legacy-pattern hit before migration commits. Post-migration, the same audit script returns zero legacy-pattern matches across `plugins/` and `.claude/`. Pre-commit hook `check-no-stack-case.sh` blocks reintroduction with documented self-exclusion list. Round-trip tests cover (a) v1 to v2 rewrite on first read with audit comment using atomic write+flock, (b) v2 idempotency, (c) edge cases — missing trailing newline, malformed YAML rejected with file+line error, comments preserved, multiple `stack=` rejected, empty `stack=` to `unknown`, EROFS graceful fallback with warn-log.

3. `commands.*` keys are multi-valued; polyglot iteration verified. Schema documents semicolon-separated lists for the listed `commands.*` keys. SC3's exercise is bounded to `commands.test_runner` and `commands.lint`; other listed keys retrofitted but not fixture-exercised in this epic. The polyglot Python+JavaScript fixture demonstrates `commands.test_runner=pytest;npm test` with both runners executing during one `validate.sh --ci` run, both results reported separately, empty trailing list elements stripped.

4. Synthetic-detector and collision behavioral tests pass with specific outcomes. `tests/fixtures/detect-fake.sh` synthetic detector emits a new namespaced tag (`platform:fake`) AND a tag colliding with an existing compound (`ruby-rails` from a non-Ruby fixture). Test asserts: (a) the synthetic `platform:fake` tag is present in consumer output without error; (b) the colliding `ruby-rails` tag from the non-Ruby fixture is deduplicated to a single occurrence in the emitted array; (c) no gate exits non-zero solely due to the collision.

5. Detector author can implement a new detector using only the published contract; documentation and dependent epics linked. A detector author can implement `detect-terraform.sh` (or any pending platform-integration detector) using only the published `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` contract, with no changes to shared consumer code; verified by the synthetic-detector behavioral test passing without modification to any consumer in `plugins/dso/scripts/`. `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` and `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` v2 published; referenced from `CLAUDE.md`. Each of 70d5-37ee, jira-dig-1582, jira-dig-1583, ee22-4785, 622a-3955 has a `depends_on` link to A0 and a one-line "blocked on A0" comment.

## Scenario Analysis

10 surviving scenarios from red/blue team filter; mitigations folded into In Scope. 1 critical scenario (mixed-state partial deploy) declared OUT (release-notes guidance).

- Auto-migration concurrent race (high, runtime) — flock + atomic mktemp/mv
- Whitespace-padded values (high, runtime) — schema-mandated strip
- commands.* embedded comma collision (high, runtime) — `;` separator
- Pre-commit hook self-trigger (high, deployment) — self-exclusion list
- Mixed state during partial deploy (critical, deployment) — OUT of scope; release-notes only
- Read-only CI checkout (high, deployment) — EROFS in-memory fallback
- Smoke run polyglot coverage (high, deployment) — SC1 explicit
- Empty `stack=` (high, configuration) — empty to unknown semantics
- Trailing empty list element (medium, configuration) — strip-empty rule
- Multiple `stack=` lines (high, configuration) — reject at migration time

## Approach

Big-bang in-place migration in one epic with explicit in-session safety nets: pre-migration consumer audit committed as artifact; post-migration audit-gate enforcement (zero legacy patterns); pre-commit hook preventing reintroduction; fixture matrix covering all stack values plus polyglot plus Strata-anticipation; auto-migration round-trip tests with edge cases; synthetic-detector + collision behavioral tests; end-to-end smoke run; pre-cutover review checklist for deep-tier reviewer.

## Dependencies

No upstream blockers. Downstream sequencing constraint: Epics A2 and B must NOT implement stack-keyed conditional logic until A0 is merged. Dependency chain enforces this (A2 lists A0 + 136b-6758; B depends on A0 + A2). If A2 or B implementation begins before A0 lands, they accept a second migration when A0's array schema activates. Soft coordination with 136b-6758 on the prompts/<topic>.md mechanism's contract — A0 records a one-line clarification comment confirming "a topic-prompt loads when its identifier appears in the stack array".
data.title: Migrate stack detection from singular value to namespaced array schema
